recent_posts.title: AGPLv3§7¶4 Empowers Users to Thwart Badgeware
recent_posts.summary: Bradley M. Kühn of the Software Freedom Conservancy explains AGPLv3§7¶4, a clause that empowers users to remove self-contradictory 'further restrictions' added by licensors to AGPL-licensed software. The post uses the current Onlyoffice/Nextcloud/IONOS dispute as a case study: Ascensio System SIA embedded a 'badgeware' logo-preservation requirement in Onlyoffice's AGPL license, disguised as a permissible §7(b) attribution term. Kühn argues this is actually an impermissible further restriction, meaning Nextcloud and IONOS's Euro-Office fork is legally entitled to strip it under §7¶4. The piece traces the history of this licensing problem from GPLv2 days through GPLv3 drafting, explains why badgeware logos are not 'reasonable legal notices,' and calls out Ascensio's aggressive response as community-unfriendly bullying.

recent_posts.title: How FOSS communities should respond to the AI coding tools influx
recent_posts.summary: Drawing a parallel to 'Eternal September' (1993's Usenet influx), the Software Freedom Conservancy coins 'Eternal November' to describe the wave of new developers entering FOSS communities via LLM-backed AI coding tools since late 2025. Rather than dismissing AI-assisted contributors as producers of 'slop', the post urges FOSS maintainers to engage with newcomers, understand their motivations, and help them build maintainable software where appropriate. It acknowledges that AI tools reduce the natural pressure to contribute upstream, and that solo forks are sometimes fine. The call to action is for FOSS project leaders to join SFC-hosted video chats to discuss adapting communities to this new wave of developers.

recent_posts.title: What the FCC router ban means for FOSS
recent_posts.summary: The FCC has banned the sale of all new home router models not manufactured in the U.S., citing national security concerns. The Software Freedom Conservancy analyzes the implications for FOSS, noting that the OpenWrt One already has FCC approval and is unaffected. Importantly, the FCC ban does not restrict users from installing their own firmware on already-purchased routers, preserving the right to run OpenWrt and other community firmware. The FCC also hints at restricting manufacturer software updates to existing hardware after March 2027, but user-initiated updates appear unaffected. SFC is accelerating efforts to demonstrate OpenWrt's compliance with NIST IR 8425A security standards and advocates for security regulations that focus on software properties rather than country of manufacture.

recent_posts.title: SCOTUS Declines to Hear LLM-Backed AI Case Regarding Copyright
recent_posts.summary: SCOTUS declined to hear Thaler v. Perlmutter, a case where an AI system was listed as the sole author of an image for copyright registration purposes. The U.S. Copyright Office and DC Circuit Court both rejected the registration, and SCOTUS' denial of certiorari leaves that ruling standing. The Software Freedom Conservancy urges the FOSS community not to panic: the ruling is narrowly scoped to cases where a computer program is identified as the sole author, and does not address copyright in prompts, LLM weights, training data, or human-modified AI outputs. The DC Circuit's own dicta suggests human authors who create, operate, or use AI tools can still hold copyright in resulting works.

recent_posts.title: Interview with Tracy Homer about Software Freedom and Maker Spaces
recent_posts.summary: Tracy Homer, Operations Manager at Software Freedom Conservancy, shares her journey with free and open source software, from initially using Linux for cost savings to understanding the importance of software freedom. She discusses how Knox Makers makerspace uses FOSS to provide accessible tools for members, her personal projects using open source tools like Inkscape and QGIS, and her work organizing the FOSSY conference. The interview highlights how software freedom enables users to modify devices, control their data, and avoid frustrating proprietary system limitations.

recent_posts.title: Some Unfortunate Delays in our Struggle for Copyleft Justice
recent_posts.summary: Software Freedom Conservancy's GPL enforcement lawsuit against Vizio has been delayed again after four years of litigation. The trial, originally scheduled for January 2025, was postponed twice in January 2026 due to court scheduling conflicts. The case centers on Vizio's alleged violations of GPL and LGPL licenses in their Smart TV products, including failure to provide complete source code, compilation scripts, and object code for relinking. The organization plans to share case documents and retrospectives while awaiting rescheduling.

recent_posts.title: A Slight Delay in our Struggle for Copyleft Justice
recent_posts.summary: Software Freedom Conservancy's GPL enforcement lawsuit against Vizio has been delayed from its scheduled January 12, 2026 trial date. The case, ongoing since October 2021, alleges Vizio violated GPL and LGPL licenses in their Smart TV products by failing to provide complete source code, compilation scripts, and object code for relinking. The trial was postponed because another older case needed more time, with a pretrial hearing now rescheduled for January 26, 2026.

recent_posts.title: Seven deaths linked to bug in Abbott Freestyle Libre glucose monitors
recent_posts.summary: Seven diabetes patients died and over 700 were injured due to a bug in Abbott's Freestyle Libre continuous glucose monitors that falsely reported extremely low glucose levels. The FDA issued a recall for affected devices. The incident highlights ongoing concerns about proprietary software in medical devices, where lack of public source code and hardware specifications prevents independent peer review by the broader engineering community. A FOSS Android application called Juggluco exists as a reverse-engineered alternative to Abbott's proprietary companion app, though most patients have agreed to Abbott's indemnifying terms of service.

recent_posts.title: Join SFC for a Q&A on how to keep your sideloading, and other phone freedom tips
recent_posts.summary: Google plans to restrict Android sideloading by blocking apps from unverified developers through Google Play Services. The Software Freedom Conservancy is hosting a Q&A session with F-Droid to help users reduce Google dependence, covering topics like removing proprietary Google code, using LineageOS, and finding free app alternatives that preserve privacy and user control.

recent_posts.title: Rethinking TikTok's future should focus on transparency and privacy
recent_posts.summary: The concern about TikTok should focus on data privacy and software transparency rather than ownership. The proposed divestment of TikTok's U.S. operations might not solve core issues since ByteDance's control over the software could persist. Releasing TikTok's source code as free and open source software (FOSS) would ensure transparency, user control, and potentially more ethical operational models, such as subscription-based services instead of data-driven ads.
